Irritable Bowel Syndrome (Psychosomatics Register · Digestive System)
Recurring abdominal pain and altered bowel habits with no detectable organic cause – the gut reacts oversensitively to stimuli of every kind.
Definition: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a chronic, functional disorder of the gut in which recurring abdominal pain or cramping occurs together with altered bowel habits – diarrhea, constipation, or an alternation between the two – without any organic cause such as inflammation, ulcer, or tumor being found on examination. The diagnosis is made when symptoms have persisted for at least three months and other conditions have been ruled out. Characteristic is an increased sensitivity of the gut's nerves (visceral hypersensitivity) as well as a close coupling to the autonomic nervous system: stress, excitement, and emotional tension often worsen symptoms immediately, while the gut tends to settle during calm, relaxed phases.
Typical symptoms: Recurring, cramp-like abdominal pain that often improves after a bowel movement; Bloating and a feeling of fullness; Diarrhea, constipation, or an alternation between the two; Mucus in the stool; A feeling of incomplete emptying; Marked worsening of symptoms with stress or emotional strain
Emergency notice: In case of blood in the stool, unintended weight loss, nighttime pain that wakes you from sleep, fever, or first onset of symptoms after age 50, seek prompt medical evaluation – these warning signs argue against pure IBS and must be checked to rule out other causes.
Every person can develop any illness, regardless of subtype. What is described here is not a diagnosis and not statistics, but a psychosomatic interpretive offering – patterns that stand out in practice, but never a substitute for seeing a doctor or licensed alternative practitioner.
Research has long called the gut the „second brain“ – via the gut-brain axis it stands in direct, two-way exchange with the central nervous system, and a large share of the body's own messenger substances for mood and tension are produced in the gut itself. In TCM, a harmonious interplay of Liver and Spleen is considered the precondition for calm digestion: when Liver Qi stagnates through withheld anger or unresolved tension, it „invades“ the Spleen and disrupts its task of processing food in an orderly way. Psychosomatic medicine often reads IBS as a gut that must literally digest what the mind cannot process – every unresolved tension gets passed directly along to it. For each of the 27 subtypes, its own pattern shows what kind of tension especially often lands in the belly.
--- Type 1: Anger the belly has to digest ---
SE1: Uncompromising self-control matters so much to the self-preservation One that anger over disorder and mistakes almost never becomes visible on the outside. The gut takes over what the mind forbids itself, flaring up with cramps in precisely the moments of greatest outward composure.
SO1: Indignation over what's wrong piles up in large quantities in the social One, since watching constantly over the rightness of things gives her plenty to object to – and she rarely says so directly. This chronically digested criticism can return as recurring abdominal cramps, right when something is once again felt to be wrong but left unspoken.
SX1: In the relationship, the sexual One gives her drive to improve things free rein – yet in especially charged moments, when criticism must for once be held back, the built-up tension can discharge as an acute, episodic cramp rather than as an even, ongoing strain.
--- Type 2: Pride that swallows its own tension ---
SE2: Exhaustion reliably announces itself in the self-preservation Two – and is just as reliably waved off, because caring for others leaves no room for a break. The gut registers what the mind blanks out, answering with cramps exactly where a pause was long overdue.
SO2: Being indispensable to many people at once costs the social Two a constant inner tension she rarely names openly. This diffuse, never fully resolved strain can show up as a gut that settles down just as little as she does.
SX2: In intense relationship phases the sexual Two nearly dissolves into the person she loves, without looking after herself at all – this pointed, highly charged tension tends to show up as an acute cramp rather than an evenly spread, chronic complaint.
--- Type 3: Achievement that leaves the belly no break ---
SE3: Digestion rarely gets the rest it needs when meals are grabbed between appointments – to the self-preservation Three, a real pause still feels like squandered time. Kept up year after year, this refusal can leave a gut that never truly settles, simply because a real pause is never scheduled.
SO3: Little recovery is left over for digestion at the pace the social Three sustains in constant comparison with others. This permanent pressure to perform can show up physically as a nervous, irritable gut that rarely rests.
SX3: Appearing successful and flawless demands real suppression from the sexual Three – bodily warning signs like abdominal pain get played down for as long as possible. This drive to control her outward image often delays paying her own belly any attention at all.
--- Type 4: Longing that cramps in the belly ---
SE4: Stubbornly and silently, the self-preservation Four, the counter-type, carries intense inner suffering without ever putting it into words. This sustained holding-back can show up physically as a gut that cramps whenever the unspoken longing finds no other outlet.
SO4: Unlike many other subtypes, the social Four rarely keeps abdominal complaints to herself – she readily talks about them and seeks sympathy for them. This open sharing can act as a valve, easing the purely physical tension in the belly even while the actual longing to be understood remains.
SX4: The sexual Four swings between closeness and despair in sharp, uncompromising bursts, living emotional intensity in the relationship without holding back – precisely these dramatic inner turns can show up as sudden, episodic abdominal cramps arising in emotionally charged moments.
--- Type 5: Withdrawal that keeps its own tension in the belly ---
SE5: Rather than seeking contact and exchange under strain, the self-preservation Five prefers to retreat – and it is exactly this withdrawal that can, on the physical level, lead to a gut that processes the undiscussed tension in her place.
SO5: The social Five meets the group by offering her knowledge while staying inwardly at a distance. This mix of participation and withdrawal can show up as a gut that rarely truly relaxes, because real closeness — even toward her own body — stays out of reach.
SX5: Unlike the reserve typical of the Five elsewhere, the sexual Five can speak quite openly about physical complaints within her one chosen, deep bond – a counterweight to the quiet suppression more typical of other Five variants.
--- Type 6: Fear that keeps the belly on alert ---
SE6: An inner early-warning system that rarely truly switches off accompanies the self-preservation Six through everyday life – this state of permanent alertness also keeps the gut under constant tension, which can show up as chronic digestive trouble.
SO6: Worry for the well-being of her group often goes unspoken in the social Six – this diffuse, collective tension can show up physically as a gut that never quite settles, reacting sensitively to any uncertainty.
SX6: Active confrontation rather than withdrawal is the sexual Six's answer to fear – this more direct discharge tends to produce pointed, intense abdominal cramps at concrete moments of testing rather than an evenly spread, chronic complaint.
--- Type 7: Excess that overwhelms the gut ---
SE7: Between appointments and pleasures the self-preservation Seven often eats hastily and irregularly, always on the lookout for the next comfort. This permanent scattering can show up physically as a gut that never truly settles, constantly confronted with shifting stimuli.
SO7: To the point of her own exhaustion, the social Seven, the counter-type, sets her needs aside in favor of others – this self-imposed overload can show up as a gut that barely ever grants itself the rest it needs to recover.

SE8: Solid control over material and physical resources secures the self-preservation Eight's existence – abdominal pain as a sign of vulnerability is ignored at first, until it can no longer be pushed away and starts limiting the reliable capacity to act she otherwise prizes.

--- Type 9: Self-forgetting that overrides its own belly ---
SE9: Comfort, fixed routines, and the consistent avoidance of any conflict shape the everyday life of the self-preservation Nine – her own digestive signals, too, are rarely consciously noticed, until they have settled into a chronic pattern hard to ignore any longer.
SO9: The social Nine seeks harmony within the group at any cost and subordinates her own voice so consistently that eventually she barely knows what she herself actually needs. This chronic self-erasure can show up as a gut that never really makes itself heard.
SX9: Hunger, fullness, and digestion often take their cue from the partner rather than from her own signals, once the sexual Nine has merged with him this completely – a fusion that makes it hard to notice her own belly in the first place.
No subtype is immune to irritable bowel syndrome, and no pattern is a verdict. What emerges is simply that each of the 27 subtypes negotiates tension, anger, and unresolved feelings in its own way – some through permanent control, others through withdrawal, self-forgetting, or an unnoticed overload of their own. This is exactly where this compass's Enneagram homeopathy begins: not with the outward symptom, but with the vital force of the respective subtype that has fallen out of balance. If this vital force – regardless of which of the 27 subtypes is affected – is brought back into balance, the symptoms can resolve holistically instead of merely being suppressed on the surface.

Acid Reflux / Heartburn (GERD) (Psychosomatics Register · Digestive System)
When stomach acid keeps flowing back into the esophagus, leaving a burning sensation that cannot permanently be swallowed away.
Definition: In gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), acidic stomach contents repeatedly flow back into the esophagus because the sphincter between esophagus and stomach no longer seals reliably. The sensitive esophageal lining, which unlike the stomach lining is not built to withstand contact with acid, responds with irritation and inflammation. Reflux is favored by excess weight, certain foods (fatty, spicy, coffee, alcohol), smoking, stress, and a hiatal hernia. Left untreated, the chronic irritation can lead to changes in the lining (Barrett's esophagus) that raise the risk of esophageal cancer – an important reason to have persistent heartburn medically evaluated.
Typical symptoms: Burning sensation behind the breastbone (heartburn), often worse after eating or when lying down; Acid regurgitation, sometimes reaching the throat; Difficulty swallowing or a lump-in-the-throat feeling; Chronic cough or hoarseness, especially in the morning; A sense of pressure or nausea in the upper abdomen; Tooth damage from repeated acid exposure
Emergency notice: In case of difficulty swallowing combined with unintended weight loss, blood in vomit, or black, tarry stool, seek medical evaluation immediately. Burning chest pain can also be a symptom of a heart attack – when in doubt, especially with radiation into the arm or jaw, call emergency services immediately.
Every person can develop any illness, regardless of subtype. What is described here is not a diagnosis and not statistics, but a psychosomatic interpretive offering – patterns that stand out in practice, but never a substitute for seeing a doctor or licensed alternative practitioner.
In TCM, an upward-striving, „rebellious“ movement of Stomach Qi is considered a cause of heartburn and regurgitation – normally Stomach Qi is meant to flow downward, so that food takes its path downward too. Emotionally, this reversal is often linked to withheld anger, frustration, or resentment that finds no other outlet and instead literally comes back up. Psychosomatic medicine often reads reflux as the picture of something that should actually have been swallowed and closed off, but keeps forcing its way back up – an anger, a hurt, or a conflict that cannot be finally digested. For each of the 27 subtypes, its own pattern shows what especially stubbornly keeps coming back up here.
--- Type 1: Anger that keeps coming back up ---
SE1: The self-preservation One swallows anger over mistakes and disorder in a disciplined way, because an open outburst does not fit her image of composure. It is precisely this repeatedly swallowed anger that can show up physically as acid forcing its way back up once the pressure grows too great.
SO1: An inner reserve of moral outrage builds up in the social One over the years, because holding it back feels easier than voicing it openly. What accumulates this way eventually wants out – showing up as chronic heartburn, an anger that can never quite be swallowed down for good.
SX1: Hardly any other subtype channels her drive to improve things into the relationship as intensely as the sexual One – when criticism must, for once, be held back in a charged moment, that tension can show up as acute, episodic burning rather than chronic, ongoing strain.
--- Type 2: Pride that swallows its own bitterness ---
SE2: The self-preservation Two regularly swallows her own disappointment and exhaustion, so as not to be a burden to others. This constant swallowing can show up physically as acid that keeps coming back up, because what actually needs to be said never finds its way out.
SO2: For the social Two, it is only natural to be indispensable to many people at once – her own hurt over a lack of recognition is rarely shown openly. This constant swallowing of genuine feelings can show up as chronic regurgitation that reports in exactly where an open conversation should have taken place.
SX2: More directly than the other Two variants, the sexual Two voices her needs during intense relationship phases – this immediate expression counters the constant, substitute heartburn more typical of subtypes that swallow their feelings instead.
--- Type 3: Achievement that leaves no time to digest ---
SE3: Eating hastily between appointments and pushing straight back into work, the self-preservation Three rarely lets her stomach finish digesting in peace. Sustained over years, this refusal to grant herself a break can surface as chronic heartburn that never truly settles, simply because rest is never actually scheduled.
SO3: A pace that leaves her digestive system almost no recovery is what the social Three sustains in constant comparison with others – this permanent pressure to perform can show up physically as a burning, irritated stomach that rarely settles.
SX3: A burning sensation in her chest gets happily played down by the sexual Three for as long as possible – appearing flawless takes priority. This focused will to control her outward image often delays paying her own body any attention at all.

SE4: Silent and unexpressed, the self-preservation Four's counter-type carries her intense inner suffering tenaciously – this sustained withholding can show up physically as a burning sensation that keeps coming back up when the unspoken longing finds no other way out.
SO4: A burning sensation in her chest rarely stays fully unspoken with the social Four. She shares her suffering with others and finds resonance in it – and this exchange can keep the underlying grief from discharging purely through the body.
SX4: Dramatic inner turns between closeness and despair belong to the sexual Four's basic emotional makeup, carried uncompromisingly into the relationship. These very turns can show up as sudden, episodic burning that arises in charged moments.
--- Type 5: Withdrawal that keeps its own bitterness to itself ---
SE5: Medical advice is something the self-preservation Five seeks only once it becomes truly unavoidable – a recurring burning sensation gets quietly endured instead. This enduring, without ever seriously treating it, fits the picture of a reflux condition that was able to settle in over years untreated.
SO5: Intellectual detachment keeps emotional closeness at bay for the social Five – so a recurring burning behind the breastbone, too, can end up filed away as an abstract fact instead of being read as a real bodily warning.
SX5: Even within her one deep bond, the sexual Five keeps control over closeness – when the intensity grows too much, she withdraws unnoticed, and it is exactly this quiet retreat that can show up as acid rising into the esophagus.
--- Type 6: Fear that shows up as sour regurgitation ---
SE6: The self-preservation Six lives in constant caution and inner tension – this permanent state can show up physically as a stomach that reacts oversensitively to any tension, producing acid that forces its way upward.
SO6: The social Six carries an often unspoken worry for the well-being of her group – this diffuse, never fully relieved tension can show up as chronic heartburn that reports in especially during phases of heightened responsibility.
SX6: Through active confrontation, the sexual Six discharges fear more directly rather than processing it through substitute reflux – this more immediate reaction counters the chronic heartburn more typical of other Six variants.
--- Type 7: Indulgences that irritate the stomach directly ---
SE7: Culinary comforts, often fatty food, coffee, or alcohol as a means of self-reward, are how the self-preservation Seven secures herself against discomfort – psychosomatic medicine reads this direct reach for stomach-irritating indulgences as one of the most immediate pictures of reflux: an esophagus that has grown accustomed to repeated acid exposure.
SO7: The social Seven, the counter-type, sets her own needs aside in favor of others, often to the point of her own exhaustion – a recurring burning sensation can easily be overlooked in the process, because attention consistently lies with the needs of others.
SX7: The sexual Seven lives out enthusiasm boundlessly, often paired with late, rich meals and intense indulgence in stimulants – psychosomatic medicine reads this impulsive intensity as one of the more direct paths to an irritated, chronically inflamed esophageal lining.
--- Type 8: Control that dismisses heartburn as weakness ---
SE8: The self-preservation Eight consistently overrides physical warning signs, because admitting weakness contradicts her self-image – a lingering burning is simply ignored until it has settled in as a chronic pattern.
SO8: Carrying responsibility for many people at once, the social Eight often puts her own health last – recurring heartburn goes unaddressed until it has quietly become entrenched.
SX8: In extreme but episodic swings, the sexual Eight lives her intensity within the relationship – this pointed dynamic differs from the chronic, structural reflux pattern more typical of permanently overridden warning signs.
--- Type 9: Self-forgetting that overrides its own burning ---
SE9: Comfort and routine are the self-preservation Nine's refuge, and her own heartburn often barely registers consciously as a result – this overlooking of a constantly recurring physical signal fits especially closely with the picture of a reflux condition that quietly took shape over years without ever being caught.
SO9: For the social Nine, group harmony consistently outranks her own voice, so much so that even her own burning sensation rarely finds real attention – this chronic self-effacement can show up as a signal that is never taken seriously yet keeps recurring.
SX9: Once the sexual Nine has merged with her partner, his perception of her health often becomes her own standard – if he does not notice the heartburn, she often does not notice it either, because the fusion with him leaves little room for her own bodily awareness.
No subtype is immune to reflux, and no pattern is a verdict. What emerges is simply that each of the 27 subtypes negotiates withheld anger, overridden signals, and its own voice in its own way – some through swallowed rage, others through withdrawal, substance-linked self-reward, or a warning of their own that is never taken seriously. This is exactly where this compass's Enneagram homeopathy begins: not with the outward symptom, but with the vital force of the respective subtype that has fallen out of balance. If this vital force – regardless of which of the 27 subtypes is affected – is brought back into balance, the symptoms can resolve holistically instead of merely being suppressed on the surface.

Stomach Ulcer (Psychosomatics Register · Digestive System)
When the protective stomach lining is damaged so severely that the body's own acid begins to injure itself.
Definition: A stomach ulcer (gastric ulcer) develops when the protective mucous layer of the stomach is damaged so extensively that the aggressive stomach acid attacks the tissue beneath it. The most common cause is infection with the bacterium Helicobacter pylori, which weakens the lining's protective barrier; regular use of certain pain relievers (NSAIDs such as ibuprofen or aspirin), heavy smoking, and alcohol consumption also favor its development. Contrary to earlier assumptions, chronic stress alone is rarely the sole cause, but it can further weaken the lining and delay healing. Left untreated, a stomach ulcer can bleed or, in rare cases, break through the stomach wall (perforation) – both serious, potentially life-threatening complications.
Typical symptoms: Boring or burning pain in the upper abdomen, often related to eating; Nausea and fullness after eating; Loss of appetite and unintended weight loss; Waking at night due to abdominal pain; Heartburn and acid regurgitation; Paleness and exhaustion from chronic, mild blood loss
Emergency notice: In case of sudden, severe abdominal pain with a board-like rigid abdomen, vomiting blood (bright red or coffee-ground-like), or black, tarry stool, call emergency services immediately – these are signs of bleeding or a perforated ulcer and constitute a life-threatening emergency.
Every person can develop any illness, regardless of subtype. What is described here is not a diagnosis and not statistics, but a psychosomatic interpretive offering – patterns that stand out in practice, but never a substitute for seeing a doctor or licensed alternative practitioner.
In TCM, the stomach is closely paired with the Spleen and is considered the place where food – literally and figuratively – gets „processed“; excess Stomach Heat is traditionally linked to pent-up anger and inner irritability. Where asthma and reflux speak of rising, outward-pressing tension, the stomach ulcer suggests a deeper, inward-directed injury: a lining that can no longer adequately protect itself, because its own acid – its own harshness toward itself – gets the upper hand. Psychosomatic medicine often reads the stomach ulcer as the picture of chronic self-criticism or inner resentment that, lacking an outer target, turns against one's own stomach wall. For each of the 27 subtypes, its own pattern shows how this harshness toward oneself arises.
--- Type 1: Anger that turns against its own stomach wall ---
SE1: The self-preservation One directs her strict inner critic above all against herself, holding her own mistakes and shortcomings mercilessly to account. This chronic self-criticism, lacking an outward-directed valve, can show up as a stomach lining that literally attacks itself.
SO1: Whoever, like the social One, constantly watches over the correctness of things, directs part of this strictness against her own inability to regulate everything perfectly. This inner reproach of not having done well enough can show up physically as burning pain in the upper abdomen.
SX1: The sexual One lives her demand for perfection with great intensity – precisely when she feels she was not good enough within the relationship, this inward-turned harshness can show up as an acute, episodic stomach pain.
--- Type 2: Pride that denies its own exhaustion ---
SE2: The self-preservation Two tirelessly looks after others and overrides her own signs of exhaustion so consistently that the neglect of self-care shows up physically – a stomach lining as unprotected as her own needs.
SO2: Admitting that her own strength does not last forever is nearly impossible for the social Two – whoever wants to remain indispensable to many people at once overrides her own exhaustion instead. This chronic depletion of herself can show up as a stomach that no longer adequately protects itself.
SX2: In intense relationship phases, the sexual Two invests herself almost completely without looking after herself – this pointed self-sacrifice tends to show up as an acute stomach pain rather than as an evenly distributed, chronic complaint.
--- Type 3: Achievement that shows itself no leniency ---
SE3: The self-preservation Three condemns any weakness or delay of her own as failure and mercilessly drives herself toward the next achievement. This lack of inner leniency can show up physically as a stomach lining that spares itself just as little as her mind does.
SO3: In constant comparison with others, the social Three directs an unforgiving inner standard against herself as soon as she falls short of her own expectations. This permanent inner reproach can show up physically as burning, boring stomach pain.
SX3: To appear successful and flawless in the relationship, the sexual Three directs sharp self-criticism against every perceived shortcoming of her own – this focused inner reproach can show up as acute stomach pain in especially charged moments.

SE4: Why her own life has to be so hard is a question the self-preservation Four, the counter-type, often asks herself unconsciously, directing reproach against herself while carrying her suffering tenaciously and in silence. This inward-turned indictment can show up physically as stomach pain that never finally resolves.
SO4: Rather than keep her pain to herself, the social Four puts it into words. This making-visible can at least partly counteract the harshness that would otherwise turn purely inward against herself.
SX4: Emotional intensity gets directed outward into the relationship, not against herself, even amid fierce swings between closeness and despair – this more direct expression tends to counteract the quiet, inward-directed self-injury of other Four variants.
--- Type 5: Withdrawal that keeps its own injury to itself ---
SE5: The self-preservation Five consistently keeps even physical complaints to herself, rarely seeking medical advice as long as it is at all possible – this quiet enduring of a boring stomach pain, without ever seriously treating it, fits the picture of an ulcer that was able to deepen over time unnoticed.
SO5: For the social Five, intellectual distance filters out emotional closeness – a recurring stomach pain, too, tends to end up filed away as an abstract fact instead of being read as a real bodily warning.
SX5: Constant vigilance accompanies the sexual Five even within her one chosen bond – the worry of revealing too much of herself keeps a baseline tension alive that can settle in as an irritated stomach lining.
--- Type 6: Fear that shows up as inner self-accusation ---
SE6: Not only outward but against her own supposed mistakes and shortcomings does the self-preservation Six direct her constant vigilance. This inner accuser can show up physically as a stomach that does not adequately protect itself.
SO6: Not having done enough is something the social Six frequently reproaches herself for, even while her worry for the group's well-being stays unspoken. This inward-directed self-criticism can show up as burning stomach pain.
SX6: Rather than turning fear into self-reproach, the sexual Six channels it outward through active confrontation – this more immediate reaction tends to counteract the inward-directed self-accusation of other Six variants.

SE7: Comforts and indulgences are the self-preservation Seven's go-to, but afterward she sometimes secretly reproaches herself for a lack of discipline – psychosomatic medicine reads this combination of direct irritation and inward-directed self-criticism as one of the more direct pictures of a stomach ulcer.
SO7: Caring for herself is something the social Seven, the counter-type, rarely permits – her own needs get set aside in favor of others, often to the point of exhaustion. This chronic inner renunciation can show up physically as an unprotected stomach.
SX7: Irregular eating, alcohol, or nicotine accompany the boundless enthusiasm of the sexual Seven – psychosomatic medicine reads this impulsive, substance-linked intensity as one of the more direct paths to a damaged stomach lining.
--- Type 8: Control that allows no weakness of its own ---
SE8: The self-preservation Eight tolerates no weakness, not even her own, and impatiently directs sharp inner criticism against every sign of vulnerability. This refusal to grant herself leniency can show up physically as an unprotected, irritated stomach lining.
SO8: While shouldering responsibility for many people at once, the social Eight tends to put her own health last – a dull stomach pain goes unaddressed until it has settled in for good.
SX8: Outward into the relationship rather than against herself, the sexual Eight discharges her intensity in extreme, episodic swings. This pointed dynamic differs from the chronic, structural pattern more typical of permanently suppressed vulnerability of her own.
--- Type 9: Self-forgetting that overlooks its own injury ---
SE9: Taking refuge in comfort and routine, the self-preservation Nine tends to barely notice warning signs of stomach pain. This overlooking of a constantly recurring physical signal fits especially closely with the picture of an ulcer that quietly took shape over years, never caught in time.
SO9: So consistently does the social Nine subordinate her voice to group harmony that her own stomach pain rarely finds real attention. This chronic self-erasure can show up as a signal that keeps recurring yet is never truly heard.

No subtype is immune to a stomach ulcer, and no pattern is a verdict. Ulcerative Colitis (Psychosomatics Register · Digestive System)
A chronic inflammatory condition of the colon's lining causing bloody diarrhea, in which the body's own defense system attacks its own gut wall.
Definition: Ulcerative colitis is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease in which, unlike Crohn's disease, the inflammation is confined to the superficial lining of the colon and typically spreads continuously starting from the rectum. The exact cause is not fully understood but is considered an interplay of genetic predisposition, a dysregulation of the immune system that attacks the body's own gut lining, and environmental factors. The disease typically runs in flares, with phases of acute inflammation alternating with symptom-free or symptom-light phases. It is classified as an autoimmune disease and requires continuous medical follow-up to recognize and treat flares early.
Typical symptoms: Bloody, mucus-laden diarrhea, often with strong urgency; Cramp-like abdominal pain, usually in the lower left abdomen; Frequent, sometimes nighttime urgency to defecate; Fatigue and weight loss during acute flares; Fever with stronger inflammatory activity; Joint pain or skin changes as accompanying symptoms outside the gut
Emergency notice: In case of severe, persistent abdominal pain with high fever, a markedly distended abdomen, or massive blood loss, seek emergency medical care immediately (a sign of possible toxic megacolon, a rare but life-threatening complication). Every acute flare should be followed up promptly by a doctor.
Every person can develop any illness, regardless of subtype. What is described here is not a diagnosis and not statistics, but a psychosomatic interpretive offering – patterns that stand out in practice, but never a substitute for seeing a doctor or licensed alternative practitioner.
Ulcerative colitis is an autoimmune disease – the body's own defense system turns against its own gut lining, in a sense mistaking its own inner boundary for an outer threat. In TCM, the function of the large intestine is closely tied to letting go and the ability to excrete what is old and no longer needed without clinging to it. Psychosomatically, ulcerative colitis often shows a pattern in which strong control, suppressed anger, and a high inner demand for order collide – a tension that, because it finds no outer expression, turns against one's own innermost boundary. For each of the 27 subtypes, its own pattern shows how this inward-directed defense reaction can arise – important throughout: here too, no one is „responsible“ for an autoimmune disease; psychosomatic patterns are interpretive offerings, not accusations of blame.

Crohn's Disease (Psychosomatics Register · Digestive System)
A chronic inflammatory bowel disease that runs in flares, can affect any part of the digestive tract, and penetrates all layers of the gut wall.
Definition: Crohn's disease is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease that – unlike ulcerative colitis, which is confined to the colon – can in principle affect any part of the digestive tract from the mouth to the anus, most often the last section of the small intestine and the colon. Characteristic is a segmental pattern with healthy sections between inflamed areas, along with inflammation that penetrates all layers of the gut wall and can thereby lead to complications such as fistulas, narrowings (strictures), or abscesses. As with ulcerative colitis, a dysregulation of the immune system plays a central role, together with genetic predisposition and environmental factors. The disease runs in flares, with longer symptom-light phases in between.
Typical symptoms: Chronic, often cramp-like abdominal pain, frequently in the lower right abdomen; Diarrhea, less often bloody than with ulcerative colitis; Weight loss and deficiency symptoms from impaired nutrient absorption; Fatigue and a general feeling of illness; Fistulas or abscesses in the anal area; Accompanying symptoms outside the gut such as joint pain, skin changes, or eye inflammation
Emergency notice: In case of severe, sudden abdominal pain with a hard, distended abdomen, high fever, or signs of a bowel obstruction (no bowel movement, no passing of gas, vomiting), seek emergency medical care immediately. New fistulas or abscesses should be treated by a doctor promptly.
Every person can develop any illness, regardless of subtype. What is described here is not a diagnosis and not statistics, but a psychosomatic interpretive offering – patterns that stand out in practice, but never a substitute for seeing a doctor or licensed alternative practitioner.
While ulcerative colitis is confined to the superficial lining, the inflammation in Crohn's disease penetrates all layers of the gut wall – a picture that psychosomatic medicine often associates with a deeper-seated, more structural injury than its more superficial sister condition. The erratic, segmental pattern too – healthy sections beside inflamed ones – can be read as an image: not everything in life is affected equally, but where the injury sits, it runs deep. In TCM, a weakened Spleen function is considered fertile ground for insufficiently processed „damp heat“ that can settle throughout the digestive tract. Psychosomatically, Crohn's disease often shows a pattern connected to deep-rooted, often long-standing injuries to one's own integrity and boundary – important here too: this reading is an offering, not an accusation of blame, and no one is responsible for an autoimmune disease. Gallstones (Psychosomatics Register · Digestive System)
Solid deposits in the gallbladder that form when components of bile harden instead of flowing freely.
Definition: Gallstones form when components of bile fluid – mainly cholesterol, less often bilirubin – harden into solid deposits in the gallbladder instead of staying dissolved. This is favored by excess weight, a fat-rich diet, rapid weight loss, hormonal factors, family predisposition, and a gallbladder that empties only inadequately. Many gallstones stay silent and are found incidentally; they become a problem when they block the bile duct and the gallbladder cramps against the obstruction (biliary colic), or when the gallbladder becomes inflamed as a result (cholecystitis). A stone that has migrated into the main bile duct can also trigger jaundice or a dangerous inflammation of the pancreas.
Typical symptoms: Sudden, cramp-like pain in the right upper abdomen (biliary colic), often after a fatty meal; Pain radiating into the right shoulder or back; Nausea and vomiting during a colic; Fullness and intolerance of fatty foods; Yellowing of skin and eyes when the bile duct is blocked; Pale stool and dark urine when bile flow is disrupted
Emergency notice: In case of persistent, severe pain in the right upper abdomen with fever and chills, jaundice, or a colic lasting longer than a few hours, seek emergency medical care immediately – this can point to gallbladder inflammation, a blocked bile duct, or pancreatitis.
Every person can develop any illness, regardless of subtype. What is described here is not a diagnosis and not statistics, but a psychosomatic interpretive offering – patterns that stand out in practice, but never a substitute for seeing a doctor or licensed alternative practitioner.
Bile has for centuries stood, linguistically and symbolically, for bitterness and withheld anger – whoever „spits bile“ or has „something rise up in their gall“ is expressing exactly that resentment which does not dissolve but settles in. In TCM, the gallbladder is closely coupled with the Liver, the organ of decisiveness, clear seeing, and unimpeded Qi flow; when this flow stagnates through pent-up frustration or chronic indecision, TCM holds that this can show up as hardening within the gallbladder system. Psychosomatic medicine often reads a gallstone as the picture of bitterness that no longer dissolves but hardens over time – a resentment that settles rather than flows. Chronic Constipation (Psychosomatics Register · Digestive System)
Persistently infrequent, difficult bowel movements – the gut holds on to what should actually be let go.
Definition: Chronic constipation is diagnosed when fewer than three bowel movements occur per week for at least three months, combined with strong straining, hard or lumpy stool, a feeling of incomplete emptying, or the need for manual assistance. Causes are varied: a low-fiber diet, too little fluid and exercise, certain medications, hormonal changes, a disturbed coordination between gut and pelvic floor, or – less often – organic causes such as narrowings. Chronic constipation is one of the most common digestive complaints overall and affects women markedly more often than men.
Typical symptoms: Fewer than three bowel movements per week; Hard, lumpy, or very firm stool; Strong straining during bowel movements; A feeling of incomplete emptying; Bloating and fullness; Abdominal pain or cramping that often eases after a bowel movement
Emergency notice: In case of suddenly onset, severe constipation with strong abdominal pain, vomiting, blood in the stool, or a hard, distended abdomen, seek prompt medical evaluation to rule out a bowel obstruction or other serious causes. Newly appearing constipation after age 50 should likewise be medically evaluated.
Every person can develop any illness, regardless of subtype. What is described here is not a diagnosis and not statistics, but a psychosomatic interpretive offering – patterns that stand out in practice, but never a substitute for seeing a doctor or licensed alternative practitioner.
Hardly any digestive symptom wears its psychosomatic reading as openly as constipation: the gut holds on to what should actually find its natural way out. In TCM, the ability to let go stands in close connection with the large intestine and the Metal element – the same element that also stands for clarity and the conscious releasing of what is no longer needed. Psychosomatic medicine often reads chronic constipation as the picture of a general pattern of holding on: to control, to old habits, to order, to possessions, or to feelings that should actually be let go. For each of the 27 subtypes, its own pattern shows what especially stubbornly gets held on to here.
--- Type 1: Anger that will let nothing go uncontrolled ---
SE1: The self-preservation One holds on to strict control over her own body – bowel movements, too, are meant to proceed in an orderly way, at the right time and without loss of control. This refusal to simply let her own body do its thing can show up physically as a gut that releases nothing not previously consciously controlled.
SO1: The social One distrusts even her own body enough to impose strict rules on it rather than trust its natural rhythm – after all, she watches over the rightness of things, including the inner ones. This demand for order can show up as a gut that lets go only reluctantly.
SX1: Even her own digestion is not spared from the sexual One's demand for perfection – it too is meant to function „correctly“, and this very expectation can make the natural process of letting go harder rather than easier.

Diverticulitis (Psychosomatics Register · Digestive System)
Inflammation of small pouches in the gut wall in which stool settles and lodges instead of being carried onward.
Definition: Diverticula are small, sac-like pouches in the gut wall, forming mainly in the descending and S-shaped part of the colon, usually as a result of years of elevated internal pressure combined with a low-fiber diet. Most people with diverticula (diverticulosis) never have symptoms. It becomes a problem when stool residue settles in one or more of these pouches, the lining becomes inflamed, and diverticulitis develops – with the risk of abscesses, ruptures (perforation), or fistula formation into neighboring organs. Diverticulitis increases markedly with age and affects a large share of people over 70 in Western industrialized nations in some form.
Typical symptoms: Persistent or cramp-like pain in the lower left abdomen; Tenderness on palpating the abdomen; Fever and a general feeling of illness; Altered bowel habits – constipation or diarrhea; Nausea and loss of appetite; Bloating and fullness
Emergency notice: In case of severe, suddenly onset abdominal pain with a hard, board-like abdomen, high fever, or signs of an acute abdomen, seek emergency medical care immediately – this can indicate a rupture (perforation) with peritonitis, a life-threatening emergency.
Every person can develop any illness, regardless of subtype. What is described here is not a diagnosis and not statistics, but a psychosomatic interpretive offering – patterns that stand out in practice, but never a substitute for seeing a doctor or licensed alternative practitioner.
Diverticula form where the gut wall gives way over years to elevated internal pressure, forming small pockets in which what should actually be carried onward settles instead. Psychosomatic medicine reads in this an image that goes beyond the simple theme of holding on: not just general holding-on, but the deliberate tucking away and hiding of things in small, sealed-off inner chambers – memories, hurts, or tasks that are not truly processed but pushed aside and left there until they become inflamed. Fatty Liver Disease (Psychosomatics Register · Digestive System)
When quiet excess accumulates in liver cells over years, without the liver itself ever raising the alarm.
Definition: Fatty liver disease (hepatic steatosis) is diagnosed when fat accumulates in more than five percent of liver cells. A distinction is made between alcoholic fatty liver, caused by regular alcohol consumption, and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), closely linked to excess weight, insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, and an unfavorable metabolic profile, and now the most common liver disease in Western industrialized nations. The liver itself has almost no pain receptors, which is why fatty liver disease can go unnoticed for years – only once inflammation (steatohepatitis) and, further along, scarring (fibrosis, up to cirrhosis) develop do noticeable complaints arise. The good news: in early stages, fatty liver disease is well reversible through changes in diet and lifestyle.
Typical symptoms: Usually no noticeable complaints at first; Occasional pressure or dull pain in the right upper abdomen; Persistent fatigue and exhaustion; Fullness after eating; In advanced inflammation: elevated liver values in blood tests; In advanced disease: weight gain in the abdominal area, skin changes
Emergency notice: In case of sudden yellowing of skin and eyes, severe abdominal pain, confusion, or fluid retention in the abdomen, seek prompt medical evaluation – these signs can point to advanced liver damage. Fatty liver disease itself is usually a silent finding that should nonetheless be taken seriously and followed up medically.
Every person can develop any illness, regardless of subtype. What is described here is not a diagnosis and not statistics, but a psychosomatic interpretive offering – patterns that stand out in practice, but never a substitute for seeing a doctor or licensed alternative practitioner.
The liver is the quietest of all the major organs – it has almost no pain receptors, never complains, and keeps working even when it is already overloaded. In TCM, the Liver is considered the seat of the Hun, the planning, forward-looking force of the soul, and the storehouse of Blood; an overloaded Liver is traditionally linked to a long-unheeded excess that accumulates over years unnoticed. Psychosomatic medicine often reads fatty liver disease as the picture of an organ that quietly and loyally absorbs everything it is asked to bear – abundance, overload, worry – without ever protesting, until the quiet excess itself becomes the burden. Celiac Disease (Psychosomatics Register · Digestive System)
An autoimmune disease in which the body treats gluten – actually a staple food – as a threat and attacks its own small-intestine lining.
Definition: Celiac disease is an autoimmune disease in which the immune system responds to gluten, the protein found in wheat, rye, and barley, with an inflammatory reaction that turns against the body's own small-intestine lining. The fine intestinal villi responsible for nutrient absorption are progressively broken down, which can lead to deficiency symptoms despite adequate food intake. Celiac disease is genetically determined and can first appear at any age, often triggered by infections, pregnancy, or other physical strain. The only currently effective treatment is a consistent, lifelong gluten-free diet – even the smallest amounts of gluten can trigger a renewed inflammatory reaction in someone with celiac disease.
Typical symptoms: Chronic diarrhea or changing bowel habits; Bloating and fullness after gluten-containing meals; Weight loss despite normal or increased food intake; Fatigue and iron deficiency from impaired nutrient absorption; Skin changes (dermatitis herpetiformis) in some patients; In children: growth delay and a distended abdomen
Emergency notice: Celiac disease itself is not an acute emergency, but persistent digestive complaints, unintended weight loss, or unexplained deficiency symptoms should be medically evaluated (blood test, possibly small-intestine biopsy). Important: gluten should not be independently removed from the diet before testing, as this can distort the test result.
Every person can develop any illness, regardless of subtype. What is described here is not a diagnosis and not statistics, but a psychosomatic interpretive offering – patterns that stand out in practice, but never a substitute for seeing a doctor or licensed alternative practitioner.
Bread has for millennia stood as a symbol of the most basic, most nourishing thing a person can take in – „daily bread“. In celiac disease, the body turns against exactly this staple food and treats it as a threat. Psychosomatically, this can carefully be read as the picture of something fundamentally intolerable – a deep, often long-standing difficulty accepting something that should actually belong to basic sustenance, whether that is food in the literal sense or care in the figurative sense. Important throughout: celiac disease is a genetically determined autoimmune disease, not a matter of character, and no one is „responsible“ for it. Hemorrhoids (Psychosomatics Register · Digestive System)
Pathologically enlarged vascular cushions in the rectum that form when too much pressure is placed on them over years.
Definition: Hemorrhoids are a naturally present vascular cushion at the junction of rectum and anus that helps provide fine sealing. One speaks of the condition only once this cushion becomes pathologically enlarged – usually through chronically elevated pressure in the abdomen, often caused by persistent, strong straining with constipation, prolonged sitting on the toilet, pregnancy, excess weight, or a family predisposition to connective-tissue weakness. Four degrees of severity are distinguished, from internal, non-visible nodules (grade 1) to permanently prolapsed external nodules (grade 4). Hemorrhoidal disease is among the most common proctological complaints overall, but is often kept silent for a long time out of shame before medical help is sought.
Typical symptoms: Bright red blood traces on toilet paper or in the stool; Itching and burning in the anal area; A weeping sensation or feeling of a foreign body at the anus; Pain, especially in advanced stages or with complications; Externally prolapsing nodules with more pronounced disease; A feeling of incomplete emptying after a bowel movement
Emergency notice: In case of sudden, severe pain with a hard, bluish nodule at the anus (a sign of thrombosis), or with stronger, persistent bleeding, seek prompt medical evaluation. Blood in the stool should always be medically investigated to reliably rule out other, more serious causes.
Every person can develop any illness, regardless of subtype. What is described here is not a diagnosis and not statistics, but a psychosomatic interpretive offering – patterns that stand out in practice, but never a substitute for seeing a doctor or licensed alternative practitioner.
Hemorrhoids arise from chronically elevated pressure – a picture that opens itself up almost immediately to psychosomatic reading: where too much has been pressed, too much burden carried, or too much endured over years without finding a counterbalance, this pressure can show up exactly at the place where the body is meant to let go, quite literally. In TCM, a „sinking Spleen Qi“ is traditionally linked to a weakness in holding the inner organs in place – an image of exhaustion that shows up in the body's lowest region. Psychosomatic medicine often reads hemorrhoidal disease as a sign of a person who withstands too much pressure over a long time, carries too much responsibility, or grants herself too little relief. For each of the 27 subtypes, its own pattern shows what pressure especially often builds up here.

Atopic Dermatitis (Psychosomatics Register · Skin)
A chronic inflammatory skin condition with tormenting itch, in which the skin as a boundary organ to the outside world falls out of balance.
Definition: Atopic dermatitis (eczema) is a chronic, relapsing inflammation of the skin that usually begins in childhood and often lasts a lifetime. It is marked by an impaired skin barrier, through which the skin retains moisture less well and reacts more sensitively to outside irritants – at the same time, the skin's immune system is overactive and responds to essentially harmless stimuli with inflammation. Typical is the itch-scratch cycle: tormenting itch invites scratching, scratching worsens the inflammation, which in turn intensifies the itch. Flare triggers are diverse – stress, certain fabrics, sweat, weather changes, allergens – but psychological state has long been considered one of the most reliable triggers.
Typical symptoms: Intense, often unbearable itching; Dry, red, scaling patches of skin; Weeping or crusted eczema during acute flares; Thickened, coarsened skin (lichenification) from chronic scratching; Preferential involvement of joint flexures, neck, and face; Sleep disruption from nighttime itching
Emergency notice: In case of signs of bacterial superinfection (strong redness, pus, fever) or sudden, painful blisters over larger areas of skin (possible eczema herpeticum), seek prompt medical evaluation.
Every person can develop any illness, regardless of subtype. What is described here is not a diagnosis and not statistics, but a psychosomatic interpretive offering – patterns that stand out in practice, but never a substitute for seeing a doctor or licensed alternative practitioner.
The skin is the body's largest organ and at the same time its boundary to the world – here it is negotiated what is let in and what is warded off, here what moves within becomes visible without. In TCM, the skin stands in close relation to the Lung, the organ that draws boundaries and lets go; an imbalance is often described as „Wind-Heat“ or „Blood Dryness“ – an excess of inner irritation that lacks the substance to calm itself. Psychosomatic medicine often reads atopic dermatitis as the story of a disturbed boundary: too much closeness that could not be warded off, too little touch that the body longs for, or an inner irritant that finds no other expression than through the skin itself. For each of the 27 subtypes, its own pattern shows how this boundary to the world comes under pressure.

Psoriasis (Psychosomatics Register · Skin)
An autoimmune condition in which the immune system attacks the skin itself, producing sharply defined, scaling plaques.
Definition: In psoriasis, a malfunction of the immune system massively accelerates skin cell renewal: instead of the usual four weeks, this cycle takes only a few days, the skin cannot shed the excess cells fast enough, and characteristic silvery-scaling, sharply demarcated plaques form – usually on the elbows, knees, scalp, and lower back. Unlike a classic allergy, the immune system here turns against the body itself. In some of those affected, the inflammation additionally spreads to the joints (psoriatic arthritis). The course is chronic with phases of varying intensity, and stress is among the most reliably documented triggers of a flare.
Typical symptoms: Sharply demarcated, reddened patches of skin with silvery-white scaling; Itching and a feeling of tightness in the affected areas; Small, pinpoint bleeding when scales are removed (Auspitz sign); Thickened, ridged, or brittle nails; Additional joint pain and swelling in some of those affected; Flares that typically coincide in time with periods of stress
Emergency notice: In case of sudden, widespread redness with fever and a feeling of being generally unwell (possible psoriatic erythroderma or pustular form), seek medical help immediately – these rare forms can become life-threatening.
Every person can develop any illness, regardless of subtype. What is described here is not a diagnosis and not statistics, but a psychosomatic interpretive offering – patterns that stand out in practice, but never a substitute for seeing a doctor or licensed alternative practitioner.

In TCM, psoriasis is frequently linked to „Blood Heat“ – an excess of inner agitation that finds no way out other than breaking through the skin. Psychosomatic medicine often reads psoriasis as the picture of self-criticism that no longer directs itself only at thoughts or feelings, but literally at the body itself – an inner judge who has become so strict that he no longer recognizes his own cells as worth protecting. Acne (Psychosomatics Register · Skin)
An inflammatory condition of the sebaceous glands, in which something builds up beneath the skin's surface and finally breaks through visibly.
Definition: Acne arises when the skin's sebaceous glands, under hormonal influence – above all androgens, but also stress hormones such as cortisol – produce increased sebum, the pore outlets become blocked by keratinization, and bacteria can multiply unhindered in this enclosed space. The result is an inflammation that can range from inconspicuous blackheads to painful, deep-seated nodules. Best known is the acne of puberty, in which the hormonal upheaval sends sebum production into overdrive, but acne also occurs in adulthood, often closely tied to periods of stress and hormonal fluctuation. Characteristic is that something builds up under the skin's surface over weeks and finally breaks through visibly.
Typical symptoms: Blackheads (open or closed) on the face, back, or décolletage; Inflamed, reddened papules and pustules; Painful, deep-seated nodules in more severe forms; Oily, shiny skin from excess sebum production; Scarring after more intense inflammations; Flares clustering during periods of stress or around the menstrual cycle
Emergency notice: In case of very pronounced, painful, deeply inflamed nodules with fever or signs of a spreading infection, seek prompt medical evaluation, as well as in case of significant psychological distress caused by the skin condition.
Every person can develop any illness, regardless of subtype. What is described here is not a diagnosis and not statistics, but a psychosomatic interpretive offering – patterns that stand out in practice, but never a substitute for seeing a doctor or licensed alternative practitioner.
Hardly any skin condition carries its psychosomatic picture so openly in its name: something builds up beneath the surface until it breaks through visibly. In TCM, acne is frequently linked to „heat in the Lung and Stomach meridian“ – an inner excess that finds no calm outlet and instead forces its way out explosively. Psychosomatic medicine sees an obvious parallel to a pent-up inner impulse – anger, shame, an unmet longing for recognition – that cannot be expressed openly and instead discharges at the skin's surface. That acne clusters especially in puberty, that phase of the greatest inner upheaval and still untrained impulse regulation, fits this picture just as well as its flaring up again in adults during especially stressful life phases. For each of the 27 subtypes, its own pattern shows what builds up here and how it breaks through.

SO1: The social One works outwardly toward a flawless, exemplary appearance, while inner irritation at her own and others' shortcomings mostly stays unspoken. This pent-up displeasure can show up as a stubborn inflammation beneath the skin's surface.

SX2: The sexual Two actively demands affection from the one important person with full intensity, rather than only quietly giving it. This open demanding stands in clear contrast to the hidden resentment of other Two variants.

SO4: The social Four likes to read her inner turmoil as a sign of special depth rather than something to resolve. This quiet elevation of her own suffering can prevent the underlying tension from actually easing, even while much gets talked about.
SX4: Fierce swings between closeness and despair belong to the sexual Four's everyday relationships, lived out unchecked and openly. This dramatic, immediate expression stands in clear contrast to the self-preservation variant's quiet, inward-directed buildup.

Hives (Urticaria) (Psychosomatics Register · Skin)
Suddenly appearing, itchy welts that can vanish again within hours – an acute reaction to something that could not be digested in the moment.
Definition: In hives (urticaria), mast cells in the skin suddenly release histamine, blood vessels become more permeable, fluid moves into the tissue, and itchy, reddened welts form that look reminiscent of contact with stinging nettles – hence the name. Characteristic is the rapid change: one welt can subside completely within a few hours, while the next is already forming elsewhere. A distinction is made between acute urticaria, which usually has a clear trigger (food, medication, infection, insect sting, but also cold, pressure, or stress), and chronic urticaria, in which flares keep recurring over weeks or months without a clear trigger being identifiable. In a substantial share of chronic cases, the cause remains unclear despite thorough diagnostics.
Typical symptoms: Suddenly appearing, itchy, reddened welts; Welts that typically subside within hours and reappear elsewhere; A burning or stinging sensation on the skin; Swelling of the lips, eyelids, or mucous membranes (angioedema) in stronger reactions; Recurring flares with no identifiable external trigger in the chronic form; Worsening of symptoms in emotionally charged or stressful moments
Emergency notice: In case of swelling in the throat or larynx area, shortness of breath, circulatory problems, or dizziness, call emergency services immediately – these can be signs of an allergic reaction up to and including anaphylaxis.
Every person can develop any illness, regardless of subtype. What is described here is not a diagnosis and not statistics, but a psychosomatic interpretive offering – patterns that stand out in practice, but never a substitute for seeing a doctor or licensed alternative practitioner.
Unlike the more chronically creeping skin conditions before it, hives is a flash: a sudden, intense outbreak that often vanishes again just as quickly as it came. In TCM, it is frequently linked to a sudden invasion of „Wind“ – an outer or inner irritant that overwhelms the skin's defenses within the shortest time. Psychosomatic medicine often reads urticaria as the picture of an acute, momentary overload: something – a word, a situation, a hurt, a contact – that could not be „digested“ or swallowed in the moment and instead pushes immediately and directly to the surface. Where atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, and acne tend to speak of slowly built-up, chronic pressure, urticaria speaks of the acute overload of the moment. For each of the 27 subtypes, its own pattern shows what could not be tolerated in that moment.
--- Type 1: Indignation that discharges in an instant ---
SE1: A sudden break in her own routine – a mistake, disorder, a loss of control – can trigger indignation in the self-preservation One that she barely lets show outwardly. This abruptly suppressed reaction can appear minutes later as a sudden outbreak of hives.
SO1: A situation perceived as unjust in her social surroundings can spark spontaneous anger in the social One that is rarely shown openly. This anger, swallowed in the moment, not infrequently finds a physical outlet through the skin shortly after.
SX1: The sexual One's indignation at perceived injustice usually erupts immediately and visibly, rather than being swallowed. This direct expression in the moment itself often makes the sudden physical detour through the skin unnecessary.

SX2: When rejected in the very moment she gives herself fully, the sexual Two tends to react with immediate, open hurt rather than quiet repression. This direct emotional outburst discharges more within the contact itself than through a bodily detour.

Rosacea (Psychosomatics Register · Skin)
A chronic vascular condition of the face with persistent redness and visible vessels – a blush that no longer fades.
Definition: Rosacea is a chronic inflammatory condition of the facial skin in which the blood vessels of the cheeks, nose, and forehead become oversensitive to stimuli and repeatedly dilate. What begins as temporary flushing with heat, alcohol, spicy food, sun, or emotional arousal turns over time into persistent redness with visibly dilated small vessels; as it progresses, inflammatory papules and pustules resembling acne but with a different cause can additionally develop. Unlike almost any other skin condition, rosacea affects almost exclusively the face – the part of the body that is most immediately visible in social contact and by which people read one another. The course is chronic, with flares closely tied to emotional and autonomic triggers.
Typical symptoms: Persistent redness of cheeks, nose, forehead, and chin; Visibly dilated small blood vessels (telangiectasia); Inflammatory papules and pustules that can resemble acne; Burning, tight, or sensitive facial skin; Thickening of the nasal skin in advanced cases (rhinophyma); Worsening of symptoms with heat, alcohol, spicy food, sun, or emotional arousal
Emergency notice: In case of additional eye involvement with redness, a foreign-body sensation, or visual disturbances (ocular rosacea), as well as rapid, painful thickening of the nose, seek medical evaluation.
Every person can develop any illness, regardless of subtype. What is described here is not a diagnosis and not statistics, but a psychosomatic interpretive offering – patterns that stand out in practice, but never a substitute for seeing a doctor or licensed alternative practitioner.
No other skin condition is so tightly bound to the face itself as rosacea – that surface by which people read one another in the first instant, where shame, arousal, and embarrassment have always shown up immediately. In TCM, persistent facial redness is often linked to „rising heat“ in the upper body, frequently triggered by pent-up emotion that finds no other way upward. Psychosomatic medicine often reads rosacea as a blush that has become permanent – as if a recurring inner arousal that once became visible only momentarily has now settled permanently into the vessels of the face. For each of the 27 subtypes, its own pattern shows what kind of arousal or exposure shows up chronically in the face here.

SE1: The self-preservation One stays outwardly composed even under inner tension – her face isn't supposed to betray her discipline. Precisely where this control matters most, a chronic redness can appear that she herself can control least of all.
SO1: Keeping public composure is part of the social One's own moral standard, even while inner anger at perceived mistakes simmers. This pent-up tension finds an uncontrollable outlet exactly in the face, her most visible surface.
SX1: The sexual One usually shows her indignation directly in her facial expression itself, brief and intense, rather than suppressing it permanently. This direct, passing reaction differs from the chronically frozen redness that tends to arise from quiet self-control instead.

SX2: Near the one desired person, the sexual Two shows her arousal openly and intensely, without hiding it. This consciously displayed, momentary blushing differs from the repressed, chronically developing variant of other Two subtypes.

SX9: How visibly aroused or embarrassed her partner seems often becomes the real yardstick for the sexual Nine once she merges with him. If he doesn't notice her own redness, the Nine often misses it too.

Vitiligo (Psychosomatics Register · Skin)
An autoimmune condition in which the skin's pigment-producing cells are destroyed and irregularly distributed white patches form.
Definition: In vitiligo, the body's own immune system destroys the melanocytes – the cells that give the skin its color through the pigment melanin. Sharply demarcated white patches of varying size form, appearing mostly symmetrically and preferentially on the hands, face, around body openings, and in skin folds. Unlike almost all other skin conditions, vitiligo usually causes neither itching, pain, nor inflammation – the color is simply missing. The course is unpredictable: some patches stay stable for years, others slowly spread, occasionally in flares that coincide with especially stressful life phases. A cure in the sense of full repigmentation cannot so far be guaranteed, though stabilization and partial repigmentation are possible.
Typical symptoms: Sharply demarcated, white, pigment-free patches of skin; Mostly symmetrical distribution, often on the hands, face, and body openings; Premature graying of hair in affected areas; Usually no pain, no itching, no scaling; Increased sun sensitivity of the depigmented areas; Unpredictable course with possible progression during stressful life phases
Emergency notice: Vitiligo itself is not an acute emergency. Consistently protect sunburn-prone depigmented, especially sensitive areas from the sun; significant psychological distress caused by the changed appearance should be taken just as seriously and treated as a physical symptom.
Every person can develop any illness, regardless of subtype. What is described here is not a diagnosis and not statistics, but a psychosomatic interpretive offering – patterns that stand out in practice, but never a substitute for seeing a doctor or licensed alternative practitioner.
Among the skin conditions in this compass, vitiligo is a special case: here nothing breaks out, nothing inflames, nothing itches – something quietly disappears. One's own color, one's own coloring, what makes the skin individual, gives way to a quiet white. In TCM, such pigment loss is frequently linked to a weakness of Blood and Kidney Essence (Jing) – a deep, slowly developed exhaustion of one's own substance. Psychosomatic medicine suggests a different direction of interpretation for vitiligo than for the previous skin conditions: not an excess that breaks through, but a deficiency, a quiet retreat of one's own color – sometimes tied to a deep loss, a grief, or the feeling of having lost visibility or one's own coloring somewhere in life. For each of the 27 subtypes, its own pattern shows what color and individuality recede here.
--- Type 1: Color that gives way to the norm ---
SE1: Flawless and even is how the self-preservation One would like her own appearance to be too – deviation is rarely tolerated, even when it happens involuntarily. The pigment-free patches of vitiligo escape exactly the kind of control she otherwise imposes everywhere.
SO1: A flawless, orderly appearance matters to the social One as proof that she counts as exemplary. Depigmented spots beyond her control can feel like a particularly painful reminder that not everything can be arranged to her own standard.
SX1: Direct, intense reactions in the moment are how the sexual One typically handles contact — little gets hidden. Visible bodily change tends to be met with this same openness, unlike the quieter self-control of other One variants.

SE2: So strongly does the self-preservation Two's attention turn outward to others' needs that her own appearance, her own coloring, barely gets noticed as its own thing anymore. This years-long stepping back of her own person can show up, quite literally, as an actual loss of skin color.
SO2: The social Two often defines herself more through her role as the group's supporter than through her own, distinctive identity. Where her own color recedes for the sake of the group, vitiligo can picture this especially vividly.
SX2: With full intensity, the sexual Two presents herself in the one relationship that matters, her own presence staying clearly felt. This active showing of herself stands in sharp contrast to the quiet fading of other Two variants.

SO3: A flawless public image is a cornerstone of the social Three's success. Depigmented patches that no training or effort can erase feel to her like a particularly hard-to-integrate attack on that image.
SX3: For the one person her attention centers on, the sexual Three wants to appear as flawless as possible – visible patches are rarely discussed publicly here, concealed instead with quiet, painstaking care.

SO4: The social Four instinctively measures her visible loss against the suffering of others in her group – sometimes feeling she suffers too little, sometimes too much. This constant inner comparison often costs more energy than the actual grief over the loss deserves.
SX4: The sexual Four lives her relationships in large, dramatic swings between closeness and despair, open and unrestrained. This outward emotional expression stands in sharp contrast to the quiet, inward loss experience of the self-preservation variant.
--- Type 5: A withdrawal that takes the color with it ---
SE5: The self-preservation Five keeps her presence in the world consistently small, retreating wherever she can. This general stepping-back of her own person can be pictured in the quiet fading of skin color.

SX9: How her partner reacts to the visible changes often becomes the real measure for the sexual Nine, once she merges with him. If the partner takes the patches in stride, it becomes easier for the Nine, too, to fold them into her self-image.

Alopecia Areata (Psychosomatics Register · Skin)
Autoimmune hair loss that produces round, bald patches overnight or within a few days.
Definition: In alopecia areata, the body's own immune system attacks the hair roots without fully destroying them – the follicles survive but temporarily stop producing hair. Characteristic is the often shockingly sudden onset: within a few days, sometimes overnight, one or more sharply defined, round, bald patches appear, usually on the scalp, more rarely on the eyebrows, eyelashes, or beard. The course is unpredictable: in most of those affected, the hair regrows on its own within months, in some the loss spreads further, and in rare, severe cases it can progress to complete loss of all scalp or body hair. A clear trigger often cannot be named, but a sudden shock, an incisive experience of loss, or a phase of intense stress strikingly often immediately precede the onset.
Typical symptoms: Suddenly appearing, sharply defined, round bald patches; Mostly painless hair loss, often noticed overnight; Short, broken „exclamation-mark hairs“ at the edge of the bald patches as an early sign; Occasional pitting or ridging of the fingernails; Possible loss of eyebrow or eyelash hair; Frequent onset following a sudden shock or incisive experience
Emergency notice: Alopecia areata itself is not an acute emergency, but should be medically evaluated to rule out other causes of hair loss. In case of rapidly progressing, extensive loss or significant psychological distress, seek prompt specialist and, if needed, psychological support.
Every person can develop any illness, regardless of subtype. What is described here is not a diagnosis and not statistics, but a psychosomatic interpretive offering – patterns that stand out in practice, but never a substitute for seeing a doctor or licensed alternative practitioner.
Hardly any symptom in this compass begins as abruptly as alopecia areata – a hole that forms literally overnight, exactly where everything was intact the day before. Hair has long been a symbol of strength, vitality, and life energy; its sudden, round loss is often read psychosomatically as the picture of an equally sudden shock, an abrupt loss of strength, or an incisive event that shook one's composure from one moment to the next. In TCM, hair stands in close connection to the Blood and to Kidney Essence; a sudden loss is often associated with a „Blood shock“ or an acute exhaustion of this substance. Unlike the slowly creeping color loss of vitiligo, alopecia areata tells of the moment itself – of the tear that suddenly appears. For each of the 27 subtypes, its own pattern shows what shock or loss of strength shows up here in a circle.

SX1: The sexual One tends to show shock immediately and intensely, right there in contact, instead of sealing it away. This direct expression in the moment often makes the bodily detour of sudden hair loss unnecessary.

Hyperhidrosis (Excessive Sweating) (Psychosomatics Register · Skin)
Sweating far beyond what the body actually needs for cooling – as if the inner alarm system stood permanently on standby.
Definition: In hyperhidrosis, the sweat glands produce significantly more sweat than is needed to regulate body temperature – often with no recognizable outer cause such as heat or physical exertion. Usually affected are specific body regions: palms, soles, armpits, or the face (focal hyperhidrosis), more rarely the whole body (generalized form). The cause is frequently an overactivity of the sympathetic nervous system, the part of the body's control system normally responsible for fight-or-flight reactions – in hyperhidrosis, however, this system stays in a kind of permanent standby, even when there is objectively no danger. Emotional arousal, nervousness, and social tension are among the most reliable triggers of acute flares. The burden of suffering is often considerable, since wet hands or drenched clothing are hard to hide in everyday and social contact.
Typical symptoms: Excessive sweating with no recognizable outer cause; Preferential involvement of palms, soles, armpits, or face; Worsening with emotional arousal, nervousness, or social pressure; Cold, moist hands despite normal ambient temperature; Skin changes from the constant moisture (maceration, irritation); Considerable psychological distress from the social visibility of the symptom
Emergency notice: Suddenly setting in, heavy sweating together with chest pain, shortness of breath, dizziness, or confusion can indicate an acute internal-medicine emergency and requires immediate medical evaluation.
Every person can develop any illness, regardless of subtype. What is described here is not a diagnosis and not statistics, but a psychosomatic interpretive offering – patterns that stand out in practice, but never a substitute for seeing a doctor or licensed alternative practitioner.
Sweat is by nature a safety valve of the body – in hyperhidrosis, however, this valve stays permanently open, regardless of whether there is actually danger or exertion. In TCM, excessive sweating is often linked to a weakness of Wei Qi, the protective defensive energy at the body's surface – a system that can no longer reliably hold its boundary to the outer world. Psychosomatic medicine often reads hyperhidrosis as the picture of a nervous system standing permanently at attention: an inner alertness that rarely truly switches off, even when nothing objectively threatens. For each of the 27 subtypes, its own pattern shows through what this inner readiness is kept permanently maintained.
--- Type 1: A tension that never quite switches off ---
SE1: Keeping self-control across every area of life costs the self-preservation One steady energy, her body staying on constant standby as a result. This permanent muscular and nervous tension ranks among the most reliable triggers of excessive sweating.
SO1: Holding a composed public front while constantly policing right and wrong inwardly wears on the social One over time. This never-quite-ending inner vigilance can show up bodily as persistently damp hands or underarms.
SX1: Tension discharges episodically and intensely for the sexual One, rather than building up permanently. This pointed release differs from the chronically steady arousal that tends to drive persistent sweating in the other One variants.
--- Type 2: An effort no one is meant to see ---
